candidates.source_title: Massive industrial warehouse being built next to the M62
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A massive industrial estate in Heywood is about to get even bigger. Construction work has started on the new 103,770 sq ft urban logistics unit coming to Birch Business Park. The new unit, called Birch 100, will be built in the south east corner of the 15.6 hectare estate. It is expected to play a part in boosting the industrial and logistics operations already in operation, situated next to junction 3 of the M66 and junction 19 of the M62 . Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The land was previously used for storage of portacabins, cranes and other construction site equipment. The tenants for the new site, McCarthy and Stone, are expected to use the new facility for maintenance of HGVs and cranes as well as a fuelling point. The scheme is being delivered by urban logistics developer and investment manager, Chancerygate, who will also refurbish three other units on the estate. Completion is expected in summer 2027. The estate sits within the Northern Gateway, a 1,600-acre employment area, straddling the Bury and Rochdale border. The Northern Gateway project is set to become one of the largest employment hubs in the region, driving substantial investment and up to 10,000 jobs into Greater Manchester. It also promises 6.5 million sqft of industrial space and new homes within areas of Bury and Rochdale along the M60 , M62 and M66 corridors. Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Head of Chancerygate’s North West office, Mike Walker, said: “Starting work on Birch 100 and completing the refurbishments mark an important step for Birch Business Park. “There is pent-up demand from business for quality, sustainable space in strategic locations across the North West. The estate can help satisfy this demand and support businesses serving the North West and beyond. “We are committed to not only delivering new urban logistics space for the region, but also refurbishing existing stock to ensure occupiers have access to high specification accommodation to meet modern-day business requirements. “We anticipate significant interest in both these new and refurbished units, so encourage any prospective occupiers to find out more about taking space at Birch Business Park.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: More than 20,000 carers who look after loved ones in the borough were thanked for all they do as more help and support for them was unveiled. The Carers’ Collaborative Event was held at Rochdale Council’s offices at Number One Riverside, hosted by Rochdale Council Adult Social Care and the Collaboration Steering Group members. The event also saw the launch of the Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale Carers’ Strategy to showcase information and support available to carers, with a particular focus on health and wellbeing. It gave carers the chance to undergo free health checks, connect with other carers and service providers in the community and access information and resources to help them in their roles. Following the event, Rochdale Council shared on its Facebook page: “Thanks to everyone who supported the council’s carers collaborative event. “The day showcased the help, support, and advice in place for the 20,000 carers living in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines and Rochdale.” READ MORE: Adult gaming centre plan for Subway after nail bar bid is pulled Carers were thanked for what they do and offered support. candidates.source_title: 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' set for clean-up in major redevelopment milestone
candidates.source_body_excerpt: 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' is a step closer to redevelopment after landowners appointed a specialist contractor to clean up the notorious former asbestos factory site. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long-held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Many locals would like to see the site transformed into a park that blends with the surrounding greenery. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement is the appointment of a specialist contractor to carry out remediation work on the site. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development.

candidates.source_title: Anselmians claim impressive win at Rochdale - Birkenhead News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Saturday saw Saints make the trip to Rochdale Rugby Club, perched on the edge of the Pennines, for their second game of the season. A fine, bright, warm day and a good pitch greeted the visitors. Injuries continue to affect Saints early in the campaign, with another three regular starters unavailable, although it was a welcome boost to see Oscar Crow and Niall Grant return on the bench. Saints made the early running, but Rochdale’s determined scrambling defence held firm until winger Sam Cotgrave barged his way over in the corner. Smith added the conversion while on kicking duties for the day. Rochdale then began to grow into the game, and with Smith shown a yellow card, the hosts took advantage. A well-worked try following missed tackles in the centre was converted to level the scores at 7-7. Rochdale missed several further scoring opportunities through dropped balls and a forward pass before eventually finding space to score beneath the posts, with the conversion giving them a 14-7 lead in front of a vocal home crowd. Saints responded well. After a penalty was kicked to touch six metres out, the resulting drive towards the line saw Joe Sanders cross for a try, with Ben Jones converting to make it 14-14. Saints continued to apply pressure, but Rochdale resisted until Olly Dodd sidestepped his defender and crossed on the stroke of half-time. Smith added the conversion on his return from the sin bin to give Saints a 21-14 lead at the break. Saints started the second half strongly, but a forced pass was spilled and Rochdale pounced, racing over in the corner. The conversion was missed, reducing the deficit to 21-19. The visitors quickly regained control. Changes in personnel helped Saints gain the upper hand in the scrum, which was beginning to take its toll on the Rochdale pack. After another attack close to the line, prop John Whittaker was driven over for a converted try, extending the lead to 28-19 and securing a bonus point. Saints were beginning to dominate possession, although Rochdale’s defence remained stubborn. A powerful scrum drive 10 metres out allowed Kincart to find Cotgrave, who slipped around his defender to score his second try of the afternoon. The conversion made it 35-19. Rochdale continued to throw everything into the contest. They were held up over the line before taking a quick tap penalty from an earlier offside offence, catching the Saints defence napping to score. The conversion was missed, but the hosts earned a deserved bonus point as the score moved to 35-24. Saints had the final say. Captain Will Grebe powered towards the line and, despite being tackled, somehow stretched out to ground the ball and score. The conversion was missed, but it completed a 40-24 victory for the visitors. It was not Saints’ best performance and they have yet to field a full-strength squad this season, but an away win and five league points represented a productive afternoon. Next up is a trip to Vale of Lune, with a 3pm kick-off. candidates.source_title: Adult gaming centre plan for Subway after nail bar bid is pulled - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton could have two adult gaming arcades within feet of each other if new plans get the green light. JR Planning Consultants has applied to Rochdale Council to turn the Subway store at 16 Middleton Gardens into an adult gaming centre. It follows an application it submitted in July to turn the premises into a nail bar. That application has since been withdrawn. In the latest application, JR Planning said the Planning Inspectorate appeal which allowed Jeffries Casino to occupy the former Virgin Money premises at 20 Middleton Gardens had set a precedent for the change of use in a retail area. It said: “The Inspector found that the proposed adult gaming centre was likely to generate greater footfall over a typical day than many potential Class E uses. “The Inspector also found that the use would provide opportunities for linked trips to shops, pubs and other town centre businesses and make a modest contribution to the functioning of the centre. “It was concluded that the adult gaming centre would form part of a suitable mix of uses complementary to the retail role of Middleton town centre. Therefore, the vitality and viability of the centre would not be undermined. “The Inspector also considered the potential concentration of adult gaming centres. It was concluded that the establishment of an additional non-retail unit would not be materially harmful to the vitality and viability of the town centre.

candidates.source_title: Town on alert as three more players pick up knocks at Rochdale - Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon Town are bracing themselves for fitness reports on three more players following their 1-0 defeat at Rochdale . Ian Holloway’s squad was down to the bare bones at the Crown Oil Arena, as Cian Hayes’ late header denied them a first away point since the opening day of the season . Swindon switched formation for the game to make a team around the available players, and there was not much help on the bench, with only James Debayo fully fit, and this was shown in the use of substitutions , as Town did not make a tactical switch until second-half stoppage time. Ollie Clarke was not initially meant to be in the squad, but he powered through a niggle and came on for Tom Nichols, who had gone down with a knock with around 25 minutes to play. Joseph Hungbo also had to be convinced to travel with the squad, as he was dealing with discomfort in his knee, but Holloway explained to him that he couldn’t lose anyone else, and so he played the final six minutes. But the possible casualties could have serious consequences for Swindon, as, along with Nichols, Aaron Drinan went down off the ball and was stretching out his hamstring before eventually being replaced, and Jack Thomson was also struggling with a cramp before he was replaced. Thomson and Drinan have been two of the players Town have relied on during this period, as both have played 90 minutes consistently. Who showed promise and who won the real duel? It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. candidates.source_title: New governor will help ease pressure on gas network - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: New equipment could be installed to help meet demand for gas in an area of Middleton. MacMarshalls Rural Chartered Surveyors & Planning Consultants has applied on behalf of Cadent Gas Ltd to Rochdale Council to install a new gas governor, kiosk and fencing next to 56 Bonscale Crescent in Middleton. The kiosk is earmarked for a corner of the open space — which also includes a children’s play area — closest to the road and against the boundary with 56 Bonscale Crescent. The application follows a previous plan to install the kiosk beside 54 Bonscale Crescent. That application was withdrawn. In planning documents submitted to the council, MacMarshalls said: “The works are driven by current pressure on the existing gas network, which means a new gas governor is required to cope with demand for gas in the local area. “Gas governors are essential to the safe distribution of gas and are designed to control gas pressure in the locality, reducing pressure from high to low in order to feed local residents and businesses. “Gas usage in the area is high from both commercial and residential end users, and the local area is therefore reliant on the gas governor, hence the requirement to install a new kiosk in this area. “The kiosk itself would not, as a standalone operation, require planning permission, as it would fall within the permitted parameters. The proposed kiosk is 26.8 cubic metres, with permitted development allowing for the installation of a structure for housing apparatus not exceeding 29 cubic metres.

candidates.source_title: Ian Holloway praises injury-hit Swindon’s effort after late loss at Rochdale - alloaadvertiser.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon boss Ian Holloway praised his injury-hit squad’s performance despite a 1-0 defeat at Rochdale. The under-fire Robins boss, who described himself as a “dead man walking” during a viral interview in the build-up to the game, felt his patched-up side deserved a share of the spoils. But Cian Hayes headed the winning goal in the 88th minute for Rochdale, three minutes after the dismissal of Kaelan Majekodunmi for a second bookable offence. “I thought it was a fantastic performance from the lads and the game turned on a couple of moments,” said Holloway. “Were the bookings really bookings? And then the ball has hit someone in the face and they score. It’s just the way it’s gone for us. “We had two good chances in the second half and we had to take one of them. Had we done that, it’s a different game. “The lads worked their socks off and it’s fine margins. One of our lads gets smashed in the head. He’s having treatment and they go and score! “It’s an absolutely rubbish rule, not everybody is cheating and lying down waiting for treatment. Why don’t they use their common sense and change the rules? My centre half is off the field receiving treatment and it should be their bloke, the one who clobbered him, who should be off the field.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale strike late to beat Swindon soon after visitors reduced to 10 men - prestwichandwhitefieldguide.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Cian Hayes headed a late winner as Rochdale capitalised on Swindon having a man sent off to secure a 1-0 victory and increase the pressure on Ian Holloway. Under-fire Robins’ boss Holloway branded himself a “dead man walking” in a viral pre-match interview but his side looked to have done enough to secure a welcome point at the Crown Oil Arena. candidates.source_title: 'Sickening' - Holloway frustrated as Swindon get no luck in defeat at Rochdale - Swindon Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ian Holloway said that it was "sickening" for Swindon Town to lose 1-0 at Rochdale after what he felt was their best away performance. Swindon were without half of their squad at Rochdale, but turned in a strong display, and would have been disappointed not to be ahead after 70 minutes as they failed to make a few big chances count. But without reinforcements on the bench, the hosts came on strong, and two yellow cards for Kaelan Majekodunmi proved too much to contend with, and Cian Hayes headed in the winner with two minutes to play. Swindon had just 15 players to pick from for the game, and it could have been less than that after Joseph Hungbo had a niggle in his knee in training before travelling. That meant that even the substitutes were not fully fit, making it an even tougher task for Swindon to end their tough run away from home, where they are still yet to win or score. Holloway said that there was so much to like about what Swindon did, but they just let themselves down at the end. He said: "That is sickening for everybody. "When you put your lives on the line like that lads did today, and there were some fantastic performances, it is tough to take.

candidates.source_title: Gut punch for valiant ten-man Swindon as they lose late at Rochdale - Swindon Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: It was heartbreak for ten-man Swindon Town as a last-minute goal saw them defeated 1-0 on the road at Rochdale. The first half was lacking in attacking quality from both sides, and Swindon will have been pleased with their ability to frustrate their hosts. Swindon started the second half very well, but a late red card for Kaelan Majekodunmi proved a bridge too far, and Cian Hayes headed home the winner. Amidst all the struggles it was a strong effort, but they are without a goal in 630 minutes of football away from home, and have taken just one point. Faced with a major injury crisis, Ian Holloway made three changes to his starting 11. Late calls were made to have Ollie Clarke and Joseph Hungbo on the bench, but they dropped out, along with Paul Glatzel, for Tom Nichols, Billy Kirkman, and Antwoine Hackford. With all the changes, Swindon went with a slightly different 4-4-2 system to try to get the most out of the available players. The ethos to have a disciplined shape that can be pressed from remained This brought an early opportunity, as Anthony Munda rushed Harvey Gilmour, allowing Tom Nichols to pounce on a loose pass. Antwoine Hackford was eventually fouled on the edge of the box, but James Ball’s free kick was tame. Swindon were clogging up the middle, but there was space for Glenn Middleton on the Rochdale left. The winger was able to run at Ball a few times early on and put crosses into the box.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale Faith News: Saturday, October 3 - inyourarea.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's faith news from the Rochdale area Last Sunday we had our joint Harvest Festival at St Barnabas Church taken by Revd Roger Hill and this week we will celebrate Holy Communion officiated by Revd Ian Stamp. The service will be followed by tea, coffee and biscuits giving us all a time to chat and get to know each other and also any visitors who are usually among us. We will meet again this Tuesday for prayer and Bible study at a member's house looking at the Gospel of Luke and finding out what the Lord has to say to us through this. As we have said before in Faith News, we have sadly reached the decision to disband our Holy Trinity Youth Theatre Workshop. We used to perform two productions each year which were very successful and have now found that we need some space so have been selling most of the costumes since we have ended the theatre group. The reason, as we have said here before, is due to the fact that the costs of producing shows have for us become rather excessive. That being said, we feel sad for the children who thoroughly enjoyed being connected with the production and the confidence that they found. Due to this decision, we still have many boxes of unsold costumes. We have been exceptionally lucky because when we decided to dispose of some costumes we found that societies throughout the world were interested in buying some. There are also some backcloths available too. We have sold some to societies in Germany, Italy, Norway and America, not bad for a little church in Littleborough. Indeed, our first Joseph and first Wizard of Oz costumes were sold to professional theatre companies in England. But our The King and I costumes have been to an American company. candidates.source_title: Details of new Scout Moor wind farm revealed
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners. The Say NO to Scout Moor 2 group has objected to Cubico Sustainable Investments plan for ‘Scout Moor 2’ ever since they were first mooted back in 2024. Campaigners fear the turbines – up to 180m including blade tip height – would be larger than Blackpool Tower and dominate the skyline. The latest changes from Cubico have seen the scheme dropped from 17 wind turbines to 12. This reduction means that the proposed windfarm would only have the potential to power 84,552 homes annually, rather than 100,000 previously touted. There is already a wind farm in operation on Scout Moor. But according to planning documents, the farm would be run separately and have a life span of around 40 years. Planning papers also highlight the need for underground cables connected to an on-site substation, which will later be hooked up to a supply point in Rossendale to deliver electricity to the National Grid. The clean energy generation from the turbines is said to recover the fossil fuel costs to build the new wind farm in 18 months. They’ve also said the excavation of peat, a pivotal carbon dioxide capture source, will be reduced by 28 per cent. Cubico has promised a peat restoration project so the extracted peat will not be lost entirely. This is something objectors don’t believe is realistic. Cubico also said they are avoiding placing turbines that dominate local viewpoints. But these statements have also been challenged by local campaigners.

candidates.source_title: Could the Turner Brothers factory finally be getting cleared up
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site – remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development

candidates.source_title: ‘No evidence that the building has been used as offices’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to keep six offices at a commercial unit have been refused because planners found “no evidence that the building had been used as offices”. Shahida Farooq applied to Rochdale Council for a certificate of lawfulness for six existing offices at Bridge House, Mellor Street, Rochdale. The property sits between Mellor Street and Spotland Road and was built over the River Spodden. It had previously been home to a private-hire booking office and light industrial use, both of which had planning permission. Mrs Farooq’s application says Bridge House has been occupied and operated as commercial offices for approximately 10 years or more, which would allow for a certificate of lawfulness to be issued. The application added: “Internal refurbishment work has commenced to subdivide the building into six individual commercial units. No material change of use has taken place as all units remain within Use Class E (offices).” A planning officer’s report stated: “There have been three planning applications associated with the site. Application 94/D30996 was for a change of use from Use Class B1 (Business Use) to Use Class B2 (General Industrial Use). Planning permission was granted subject to conditions. “Following this, there were two applications in 1999 for the use of the basement as a private-hire booking office and a retrospective application to site a portacabin for use as a private-hire booking office with associated parking and external water closet. “Google Streetview images from August, 2016, of the front elevation facing Mellor Street show that there were two units. The fascia signs read Langstreth & Hunter Accountancy Service and Conservatory & Garden Furniture.

candidates.source_title: Oldham to Rochdale Tram Line - Premier Construction News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed, marking a major milestone in this summer’s programme of network improvements. The work, which took place over a planned two-week closure between Victoria and Rochdale town centre, is part of a wider £150m investment to maintain and improve Greater Manchester’s tram network. It will help deliver a smoother, more reliable service for passengers and support the long-term resilience of the network. Engineers worked day and night between Monsall and Newton Heath & Moston to replace 1.2km of track, improve drainage, renew foundations and correct the alignment and level of the track. It was a big and complex job, using around 290 new concrete sleepers, 2,000 tonnes of gravel and replacing more than 5,000 tonnes of ballast. As a result, sections of the route that previously required speed restrictions can now return to normal operation – up to 50mph on some sections – helping to improve journey times for customers. Ian Davies, TfGM’s Network Director for Metrolink, said: “This was a large and complex piece of engineering, that will make a real difference to the reliability and long-term condition of the network. “It’s the first major milestone of a wider programme of improvements we’re delivering across our tram network this summer to keep it safe, resilient and fit for the future. “We know closing a line is disruptive, and we’re very grateful for everyone continuing to bear with us while this essential work is completed.” Further improvement work will take place at other locations across the Bee Network over the coming months. The most significant being at Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield. While this work is carried out, there will be no trams on the Eccles, Trafford Centre or Altrincham lines for three weeks from Monday 13 th July to Sunday 2 nd August. Before that, further tram improvement work took place in the city centre . Further work to finish off the job on the Oldham-Rochdale line also took place on Sunday 7 th June and Sunday 12 th July. Further information on tram improvement works can be found here: https://tfgm.com/tram-improvement-works
